relevance_note: Historical layerwise offload route: establishes that heterogeneous specialized execution predates recent coding agents.
target: Models exceeding GPU memory and throughput-oriented workloads that tolerate large batches or sequences motivate layerwise offload and transfer/computation overlap.
mechanism: Hosts weights in CPU or NVMe memory and streams them layer by layer to GPU, using prefetch and large token batches to amortize transfer costs while preserving GPU memory for activations.
caveat: ZeRO-Inference is a throughput-oriented offload path within DeepSpeed; the published KV-offload example requires model-specific changes and a Transformers fork, and capacity does not imply low interactive latency.

relevance_note: Heterogeneous MoE execution route: compare CPU expert computation with transfer-centric designs.
target: Small-batch local Mixtral-8x7B inference and GPU memory smaller than the unquantized model make activation transfer cheaper than expert-weight transfer.
mechanism: Executes uncached MoE experts on CPU by transferring small activations instead of moving their large weights to GPU, while keeping selected experts resident on GPU.
caveat: The official prototype is limited to 16-bit Mixtral-8x7B and relies on PyTorch CPU expert execution; the README explicitly calls out poor CPU performance without AVX512.

relevance_note: A model-specific implementation links disclosed AI-assisted construction to SSD expert streaming and explicit approximation choices.
target: The implementation targets Qwen3.5-397B-A17B on Apple unified-memory hardware with SSD capacity far exceeding RAM and fixed model geometry.
mechanism: Streams selected quantized expert blobs with parallel pread and executes a fixed Qwen hybrid-attention pipeline using custom Metal dequantization and fused expert kernels.
caveat: The source states the model has ten active experts but the executable uses K=4, so its reported speed is not an equivalent top-10 baseline; the README also reports broken tool JSON for its 2-bit mode.

relevance_note: Throughput-oriented offload route: a comparison for existing memory scheduling and workload trade-offs.
target: Throughput-oriented workloads with large effective batches, limited GPU memory and available host/SSD capacity expose the latency–throughput trade-off.
mechanism: Uses a block generation schedule and GPU/CPU/disk tensor placement to reuse layer weights across microbatches while overlapping transfers and optionally compressing weights and KV state.
caveat: This is an OPT-centric throughput/offload implementation, not evidence of interactive low-latency performance for arbitrary contemporary models; the repository is now named FlexLLMGen.

relevance_note: A substantial heterogeneous backend provides a core case for rebuilding execution while retaining shared serving infrastructure.
target: CPU AMX/AVX capabilities, NUMA topology, GPU memory and expert precision constrain the heterogeneous placement and execution backend.
mechanism: Runs memory-heavy MoE experts through ISA-specific CPU kernels and NUMA-aware placement while integrating with GPU serving runtimes for the remaining model computation.
caveat: The current repository exposes kt-kernel inference and separate fine-tuning capabilities; legacy YAML-injection examples and training speedups should not be generalized to its current serving path.

relevance_note: Expert-offload route: compare established prefetch and residency policies with separately reconstructed runtimes.
target: Sparse expert activation, per-model offload stores, GPU-memory budgets and model-specific resident tensors constrain caching and transfer decisions.
mechanism: Offloads expert weights to host memory and SSD, retains hot experts in an activation-aware GPU cache and uses trace/prediction-driven prefetching through a native transfer engine.
caveat: The public HuggingFace-friendly implementation differs from the paper system; some configuration flags are reserved or scaffolded and DeepSeek MLA does not automatically use FlashInfer acceleration.

relevance_note: A narrow MoE runtime makes expert placement and execution choices inspectable; AI authorship is not established.
target: The Qwen3.8-Flash-Next model family, supported quantized layouts, consumer GPU VRAM and CPU memory/bandwidth define expert residency and transfer-versus-compute choices.
mechanism: Keeps attention and hot experts on GPU, computes nonresident experts on CPU concurrently, and budgets GPU/RAM/file tiers for experts and long-context KV state.
caveat: The documented route-tail-skip path is enabled by default in eligible CUDA and some HIP configurations and drops low-ranked missed experts; CPU/GPU rounding and changing residency can also change outputs.

relevance_note: General-engine reference for the VibeQwen construction case and upstream serving infrastructure retained by the Radiance specialized backend.
target: Variable request lengths, overlapping prompts, finite KV capacity and layer-specific attention/state layouts determine block ownership and admission.
mechanism: Manages attention state as pooled KV blocks with reference-counted prefix sharing and schedules token-budgeted work across requests, allocating cache slots as execution advances.
caveat: Paged KV management is one subsystem in a broad runtime; prefix reuse requires matching cache identity, and hybrid attention/state models need distinct cache rules rather than a universal layout.

caveat: Lossless refers to the already-ternary model representation, not conversion of an arbitrary FP16 LLM without quality change; supported model/kernel pairs differ by platform.

caveat: A reusable diagnosis workflow rather than a kernel generator or inference runtime; counter names and heuristics require device-specific checking, and suggested fixes need measured validation.

relevance_note: Operator-level construction harness connecting coding agents, measured feedback, acceptance gates and reusable optimization knowledge.
target: Evaluator-owned GPU operator tasks, target DSL/device and fixed optimization budgets constrain candidate search and acceptance.
mechanism: Runs coding episodes in isolated worktrees, evaluates numerical and performance results before promotion, and uses profiler feedback plus scoped GPU Wiki retrieval to guide further revisions.
caveat: Produces operator kernels, not a complete inference engine. Fast and full episodes use different measurement gates; production policy and finite numerical probes do not prove arbitrary-input correctness. GPU Wiki is a component of this record, not another repository count.

relevance_note: Production-derived operator tasks and separated evaluation provide a benchmark for generated execution components.
target: Production-trace operator shapes, executable PyTorch references and target GPU/DSL determine the generation and evaluation contract.
mechanism: Packages reference programs and input/shape generators, separates agent-visible tasks from evaluator metadata, and checks compilation, numerical outputs/input mutations and forward timing against a roofline estimate.
caveat: End-to-end refers to operator generation and evaluation, not a complete serving stack; correctness uses finite inputs and tolerances, and roofline efficiency is not an application-level speedup.

relevance_note: Retrievable hardware and kernel experience connects prior engineering work with subsequent specialized implementation decisions.
target: NVIDIA Blackwell / Hopper kernel programming, hardware features and version-specific CUDA/DSL behavior delimit the knowledge corpus.
mechanism: Indexes upstream PRs, hardware documents and optimization notes with architecture/symptom filters, and links synthesized pages to captured kernel artifacts and provenance.
caveat: Kernel-level knowledge support rather than an engine or proof of lower development cost. Corpus cutoffs and source confidence matter; included assets retain upstream licensing and are not independently reproduced by this survey.

relevance_note: Concrete hardware-investigation knowledge and accepted/rejected experiments feed the separately cataloged ane.cpp engine.
target: Empirical Apple M3 Max ANE behavior, private framework APIs and Qwen-family execution motivate targeted probes.
mechanism: Uses small MIL/ANE probes and CPU-reference checks to investigate execution limits, records kept and discarded experiments, and transfers supported findings into ane.cpp.
caveat: Findings and timing reports are author-measured and primarily M3-Max-specific; private APIs may change. This is a knowledge/probe resource linked to ane.cpp, not an additional inference engine.

relevance_note: Sustained agent-driven reconstruction of an existing inference engine connects inherited code and reports to kernel, runtime and decoding changes; the study also exposes gaps in its evolving validation gates.
target: The paper centers on Qwen3-0.6B on one H100 with single-request greedy decoding, with supplementary Llama-3.2-1B experiments. The linked public ten-trial example uses RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell and is a separate configuration.
mechanism: Keeps the coding agent fixed while successive sessions inherit and revise engine code and reports; the paper also exchanges discoveries across chains. Changes span quantized kernels, fusion, CUDA Graph execution, scheduler/state handling and prompt-lookup decoding.
caveat: The paper reports 3.27x natural-request throughput on H100; the linked public demo reports 512 to 1016 tokens/s on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell. Do not conflate these artifacts or budgets. Quantization changes numerics, finite gates do not prove equivalence, and the public ten-trial driver does not establish availability of every paper experiment or synchronization protocol. No independent execution was performed here.

relevance_note: Connects generation-time model/hardware/workload specialization to a concrete serving-system initiative; the broader generator and its scenario-specific outputs are distinct artifacts.
target: The VibeServe initiative studies target-specific language serving, streaming ASR, constrained output, multimodal workloads and Apple Silicon. The current VibeSys repository also serves non-inference domains, which are outside this record.
mechanism: Separates design search from implementation and target-specific measurement; durable history carries hypotheses while framework-owned evaluation identities and candidate isolation connect code changes to reviewed results.
caveat: The May 2026 VibeServe paper and the October-reviewed VibeSys implementation are not identical revisions. Results concern selected scenarios and declared contracts, not arbitrary serving workloads or proven lifecycle savings. Evaluation wiring was source-inspected; no agent campaign or generated engine was executed.

relevance_note: A model-program construction case combining a restricted agent edit surface, deterministic lowering and schedule checks; contrasts with unconstrained whole-runtime generation.
target: Supported HuggingFace Llama-family graphs on CUDA, principally batch-one decode. Paper speed sweeps at position zero use synthetic weights at real model shapes; real-checkpoint quality tests have a separate scope.
mechanism: Lowers model graphs through a typed task/counter IR to one cooperative CUDA launch per forward pass. Agent-facing loops tune instruction implementations or structured schedules, with static IR checks and reference evaluation.
caveat: Static graph checks rely on a trusted VM and supported IR, not a mechanized whole-stack proof; inspected data-hazard checks have a task-count cap. Reported W8A16 wins compare against bf16 and cannot establish equal-precision superiority. The host still drives token steps; this is not a complete concurrent serving engine.

relevance_note: An industrial platform-specialization case documenting why a provider rebuilt execution instead of only configuring a general framework; useful without an AI-development attribution.
target: Cloudflare distributed inference nodes with constrained host CPU, startup and isolation requirements. The initial Hopper-focused report and later large-model/multi-GPU update describe different deployment stages.
mechanism: Rebuilds the Rust HTTP, batching and execution path; overlaps model loading and model-specific kernel compilation, manages paged state and cached execution graphs, and later adds pipeline/tensor/expert parallelism.
caveat: The engine is proprietary; evidence is official engineering disclosure rather than source inspection or independent reproduction. Initial CPU/performance comparisons mix bare-metal and sandboxed deployment conditions. Later multi-GPU support must not be treated as present in the initial release.

relevance_note: An industrial model/runtime/hardware co-design case with an explicitly narrow low-latency operating point; distinguishes a purpose-built execution architecture from a generic serving configuration.
target: The reviewed low-latency preview uses an FP16 approximately 2B Laneformer model, batch one and eight AMD MI300X GPUs; the companion announcement also reports an eight-H200 configuration.
mechanism: Co-designs a persistent device-side generation loop with weight streaming, sampling, topology-aware handoffs and Laneformer delayed tensor-parallel communication, according to the vendor engineering report.
caveat: The review covers vendor documents, not public engine source or reproduced results. The headline preview combines Laneformer/DTP with an eight-GPU FP16 setup; it is not evidence of the same gain on an unchanged arbitrary model, and third-party model roadmap statements are not implemented support.

relevance_note: Specializes decoding, state refresh and serving for diffusion language models instead of treating denoising as autoregressive token generation.
target: LLaDA 8B, LLaDA-MoE 7B and LLaDA2 mini/flash families on qualified NVIDIA multi-GPU paths.
mechanism: Combines diffusion-iteration and confidence-based block decoding with configurable KV refresh, batch handling and compiled/CUDA-graph execution, integrated through vLLM or SGLang adapters.
caveat: The paper's headline H800 result and any model-versus-AR comparison depend on model, precision, decoding policy and hardware; they do not isolate an engine-only gain. Partial KV updates can change semantics. Some committed GPU tests reference private checkpoint paths, and no GPU reproduction was performed.

relevance_note: Turns the VDN-H3 video generator into an adaptive local execution path with request-specific residency, precision and attention choices on constrained consumer devices.
target: VDN-H3 eight-step MiniMax H3 video generation on qualified consumer NVIDIA GPUs; Apple-Silicon support is a separately qualified preview.
mechanism: Plans transformer/VAE block placement across VRAM, pinned RAM and disk from live capacity, selects int8 or FP8 paths and probed attention kernels, then streams nonresident weights with bounded prefetch.
caveat: The claimed 8 GiB VRAM/16 GiB RAM path is tied to the VDN-H3 checkpoint and request plan, not general MiniMax H3. The pre-distilled eight-step checkpoint, int8/FP8 execution and quality presets change model/precision assumptions. Model weights have a separate restricted license; published capacity tests do not prove all devices or output quality.

relevance_note: Rebuilds Colibri's disk-streamed MoE architecture around concurrent I/O, CPU and optional CUDA lanes, with a measured same-hardware comparison exposing when the rewrite does not help.
target: GLM-5.2 744B-style int4 MoE streaming on Linux with NVMe, CPU and optional NVIDIA CUDA expert execution.
mechanism: Uses completion-driven io_uring expert reads, CPU compute workers and an optional GPU lane against routed-expert work lists, reducing in fixed order and sharing batch-union expert loads.
caveat: Author measurements on a disk-bound RTX 3060/Ryzen setup report slower single-sequence decode (0.062 tok/s) than Colibri (0.077 tok/s), despite concurrency gains in some batching and I/O experiments. CUDA is feature-gated and hardware validation is separate; source inspection and documented tests are not independent reproduction.
